end.summary:
Practised representing square numbers with dot arrays: 2×2, 3×3, and 5×5.
Explained the growth from an n×n square to an (n+1)×(n+1) square using a new row and column.
Used overlap to calculate added dots: 2n+1; applied it to 4×4 to 5×5 and 12×12 to 13×13.
Connected the added dots to an L-shape; triangular-number pictures were not demonstrated.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised drawing square-number pictures and explaining how a square grows by adding one row and one column. They correctly accounted for the shared corner and used 5+5−1=9 and 13+13−1=25, then stated the general rule 2n+1. At home, you can draw a 3×3 or 4×4 dot square and ask Ishita to show and count the added L-shape when growing it by one row and column.
